absent: How backing page allocation behaves under memory pressure, including reclaim, compaction, placement and exact failure conditions beyond null return.
Locking discipline during table use, including acquisition ordering, nesting, interrupt safety and required hold times for page table locks.
TLB flush and RCU reclamation mechanics, including when queued tables become reusable and how batch saturation interacts with concurrent faults.
Architectural entry encodings, actual shift and index calculations for non-folded levels, and concrete page size values.
Accounting semantics for pagetable usage counters and their visibility outside memory management.
Userfault write-protect marker semantics on architectures with native support, beyond the generic neutral stubs.
Allocation hook behaviour wrapping the public entry points, including tracing and profiling effects.
Recovery behaviour for misaligned frees beyond fatal trap, and any debug support around it.

findings.text: Generic code supplies a kernel PTE table allocator that, for a caller supplied address space, yields either a usable zeroed table marked as kernel owned or a null failure signal when backing storage or construction cannot be completed.

Generic code supplies user PTE table management where allocation accepts address space plus caller flags or defaults to accounted user flags and reports a page wrapper or null, while release accepts address space plus table reference and runs destructor then release.

Allocation for PMD, PUD, P4D and PGD levels shares one contract: the initial address space selects kernel flags and kernel marking while other spaces use accounted user flags without that marking, PGD alone accepts a variable order, and any failure surfaces as null.

Release for PMD, PUD, P4D and PGD levels accepts address space plus table pointer, requires page aligned input, runs shared destructor then release, and P4D release is skipped entirely when the level is folded for the given address space.

A shared pagetable core manages descriptor backing: allocation obtains compound capable storage, per level constructors establish lock state plus share count plus table marking plus usage accounting, and destruction reverses accounting plus marking plus lock state before freeing.

Generic TLB gathering offers table and page removal where immediate table release runs full teardown, deferred table release runs only destructor then queues the backing page, and page removal defaults to one base page with flush triggered when the gatherer reports saturation.

With P4D folded the PGD level reports empty and bad as false and present as true with clearing and population as no-ops, offset is identity, allocation yields null with release as no-ops, and range helper returns its end.

With PMD folded the PUD level reports empty and bad and user and leaf as false and present as true with clearing and population as no-ops, offset is identity, allocation yields null with release as no-ops, and range helper returns its end.

With PUD folded the P4D level reports empty and bad as false and present as true with clearing and population as no-ops, offset is identity, allocation yields null with release as no-ops, and range helper returns its end.

Generic userfault write protect helpers are neutral: query helpers report unsupported or absent, and set or clear helpers return their input unchanged for both present and swap forms at PTE and PMD levels.

Page, folio and pagetable descriptor are alternative views of one backing object, so conversions among them are type reinterpretations without address change, and virtual address derivation flows from descriptor through folio and page to low memory mapping.

A single kernel ownership flag distinguishes kernel tables from user tables: it is set after successful kernel allocation, consulted to choose the free path, and cleared before backing release for symmetry.

The initial address space bypasses per table lock establishment and uses kernel allocation parameters, while all other address spaces attempt lock establishment and use accounted user parameters, with lock failure causing descriptor release and null report.
Order discovery treats lack of head marking as order zero and otherwise exposes a low byte of auxiliary flags as the large order, allowing release to free the correct span.

Folded levels collapse to one entry by aliasing shift to the parent shift and deriving size and mask from that shift, with wrapper types holding a single parent entry and value conversions delegating to the parent.

Folded accessors delegate to the parent level: setters forward to the child setter, numeric conversions unwrap then rewrap the parent value, and page address helpers forward through the child page helper, with error helpers forwarding similarly.

Per table locking has two builds: one where lock allocation always succeeds and the lock is either pointed to or embedded with explicit initialization, and one where initialization and release are trivially successful no-ops; PMD adds optional huge entry clearing plus share count reset before delegating to the common path.

Table batching uses a header with optional RCU linkage plus a live count followed by a flexible array of table pointers, with capacity determined by how many pointers fit in one base page after the header.

Page gathering uses batched nodes linked together, each carrying live and maximum counts plus a flexible array of encoded pages, with a small bundle constant and derived limits for per batch capacity and total batch count.

A pagetable descriptor moves among unallocated, allocated but unconstructed, ready for use, destructed, and released; construction failure returns to released with null, and the two removal paths differ only in whether release is immediate or queued via the gatherer.

The gatherer stays in accumulating state while removals fit and transitions to flushing when a removal reports saturation, after which accumulation resumes; single page removal is expressed as size qualified removal with base size.

Public per level entry points wrap internal no-profile helpers with allocation hooks, exposing kernel and user PTE creators plus PMD, PUD, P4D and PGD creators that callers use without referring to the internal variants.
Freeing upper levels demands page aligned pointers and treats violation as fatal, so callers must only pass tables as originally allocated and never interior or unaligned addresses.
Debug builds verify that fresh descriptor lock storage reads as zero before initialization, treating nonzero as a fatal slab reuse conflict where table storage was previously used for slab metadata.
Generic TLB handling conservatively requires table invalidation on every removal while synchronization helpers are empty, so implementations must not rely on those helpers to order reclamation.
Kernel table allocation combines base kernel reclaim behaviour with zeroing and KASAN skipping, and user table allocation adds accounting on top of that kernel combination.

Folded levels publish a single entry count with shift aliasing to the parent, size as one shifted by that shift, and mask as negation of size minus one, plus a folded marker for conditional compilation.

Gathering publishes a small fixed bundle size with batch capacities computed from base page size minus header divided by entry size, and a total batch count derived from a fixed entry budget divided by per batch capacity.
Reverse mapping delay has two configurations: one records delay in the gatherer and always reports success, the other never delays and provides an empty range flush.
Non-maskable interrupt user access checking is unconditionally approved in the generic header, imposing no additional gating on such accesses.
Each generic header defines a single inclusion guard macro that prevents repeated processing of its declarations within one translation unit.
Whether P4D is folded for an address space is decided solely at compile time from the folded marker, without inspecting the runtime address space argument.
